Runaway 3 decided to do a 180° turn and focus on a gritty, realistic story and complex, but solvable puzzles, while leaving the vivid colours behind. If you enjoyed the craziness of the first two games for some reason, you may be appalled how “normal” this one is.
Runaway: A Twist of Fate feels almost like as if it isn’t even the part of the same series ‘The Dream of the Turtle’ was. It even starts by stating almost none of the events of the previous game ever happened, but it doesn’t stop there: the first game’s plot is reduced to a tale the protagonist cooked up in his head to justify stealing 20 million dollars from the mob.
Runaway 3 is, in short, an on-the-run thriller, where Brian and Gina are trying to disappear from the military police of the second game and from the mob they scammed in the first game– packed into a relatively tame but good-looking point ‘n’ click adventure game.
No more immature sex jokes, only humour that knows its place and the importance of timing in delivery. No more super spies, only mob enforcers. No more Joshua… thank all deities.
Also, no more bad voice acting. Almost the entire cast was replaced with people who can act, all this to put a larger emphasis on the more serious tone. This realism is also present in the scenery: the jungles and military bases are replaced with more everyday locations like alleyways, an asylum, or a cabin in the woods (where you conduct a rather normal investigation into a murder case).
The puzzles are less Gabriel Knight 3 and more Broken Sword 1. Everything you do follows point ‘n’ click logic, but it
have logic and structure.
Essentially, Runaway 3 was changed into an average adventure game that doesn’t really do much to stand out, but it also means it stopped being the colourful, annoying clown that probably hurt the good name of this genre more than it helped.

-Settings menu is pretty sparce
-Slow (More of a preference)
-Enemies that aren't tough mainly just have a lot of health or you just take too much damage

While the cons seem to outweigh the pros, it's not that bad of a game. I've been playing this game since the early betas and I have mixed feelings about the finished product.  Though simple, the beta interface seemed easier to both see and use and the graphics, in my opinion were better back then.  I'm glad I kept one of the beta builds from when the game was being developed so that I can play that version over this one.  Notably, this is not to say that this game is bad, but it is very short and I'm not sure I like how it ended up.
So, the things I like about the game are the exploration elements...and that's just about it.  It's not a particularly good strategy game and unless you get really good luck with the randomizer, the enemy will almost always have the advantage in battle, meaning you avoid or retreat from fights a lot.  While there aren't a huge amount of things to indicate what is better than other things equipment-wise, you can rest assured that if an equipment or item says it does something, it most likely does it some way or another.
Things I don't particularly care for are many.  They are all minor things that altogether don't make the game not worth owning or playing, but they are annoyances I can't say I like.  As mentioned above, you are largely at the mercy of the randomizer.  If you get mediocre or bad item drops, you can expect to blow up at some random time or your first attempt at battle.  The variety of equipment and weapons seems significantly smaller than in the betas.  I don't know if that's true or I simply haven't encountered many of them since I started playing again.  The graphics seemed to get a downgrade for the most part, even the pictures of cats that were used as stand-in images for things that hadn't been completed yet were better than some of the final art we got.  In the beta, items had some stats you could compare to see what was better than what and gave a lot of insight on how you might want to equip your ship.  That information is now gone, making outfitting your ship rather tedious when you realize that, though something had a better rating in coins, it ended up hurting your strategy pretty significantly when you tried it in battle.
It seems like they realized they wouldn't be finished with the game anytime soon and gutted out the parts that they hadn't finished yet and then simplified a lot of graphics to finish it up.  The three ships you get to choose from at the start are all there are and they don't really affect gameplay much.  Overall, while not a bad game, it's very lackluster, nonetheless.  I had high hopes for this title, but I would have to say that I was disappointed with the end result of all that time spent in beta.

PvP playtime:
PvE playtime:
TL;DR: This game was in Limbo. It was in a bad state, but came out of it very well! At the moment it's worth while giving it at least a try. It's much improved over the past 12 months.
Pro's:
1. No premium ammo. But very varied ammo that has very different characteristics: Sabot, PELE (sabot), HEAT, HESH (HEP), HE (FR).
2. Many Different vehicles that have various weaponry: Guns, Auto Cannons, ATGM's and Recoilles Rifles.
3. Advanced armor like: ERA, Cage and APS.
4. Many different retrofits.
5. In-depth commander system (Crew system will be overhauled too)
6. Premium vehicles are note P2W, fairly affordable and are balanced accordingly (but have some preferencial MM.)
7. Progression is fairly quick early on but proves a longer grind in higher tier.
8. PvE and GLOPS gamemodes next to 15v15.
9. No Arty in PvP and GLOPS.
10. A very responsive Discord community with active mods.
Con's:
1. PvE is still the same gameplay as it used to be
2. Graphically demanding on your GPU.
3. 32GB download.
4. Retrofits are expensive and more for high end users.
5, Events are sometimes a bit mismanaged.
6. Patches have been far apart and feel buggy before being fixed.
7. MyCom feels disconnected from the playerbase at times. (the voluntairy mods on the contrary are in touch via discord and the forums pretty well.)
Bottomline: This game has come far although it had it's issues and controversial moments. In the end this game is heading in a good direction and development actually takes player feedback into account although it doesn't look like it at times.

This game is not worth $44 CAD. I picked it up on sale for -50%, and I'm still ambivalent about the whole thing.
Let me start off that while the game isn't perfect, it's not bugs or gun play that are going to kill your desire to keep playing it. Oh, no. Instead, SQUAD suffers from one of the age old issues of online gaming:
I've had one or two GOOD games, where the squad leader really knew what he was doing, people cooperated, and I got to feel like I'm doing something other than wasting my time. In the one game I barely even fired a shot - I played medic - yet it was still a satisfying experience.
But in ALL THE OTHER GAMES, which constitute around 13 hours of gameplay, I've felt frustrated and powerless. I've gotten banned from a team for asking the leader what the plan was. Heck, I just dealt with a guy who would answer every question with "Watch my twitch account! It's *bla bla bla*!".
"But Andrei", you'll say, "you've just had a run of bad luck! Keep playing, it'll get better."
Well, here's the deal. These are not short games. You're joining for 40 or 50 minutes, on average. The game involves running around large maps, and often a large part of the gameplay is simply getting from one point to the other (which is mind numingly boring). And it really sucks when at the end of that 5-10 minute walk you get killed out of hand, because your team lead didn't set up defences, or organize the assault.
I don't have the time to invest 10 hours into a game in the hope of getting 1 hours of fun out of it, and I'm not sure I envy the people who do. Unfortunately the game lacks a system to rank players, and so it's always a complete roll of the dice whether you'll have a decent time or not - and the deck is definitely stack against you.
And so, beware all who are interested in SQUAD. Playing this game involves A LOT of frustration, and a LOT of time spent trying to find a decent squad to play with.

(After this review is a recountment of my first hour of playing)
The SKIES is a pvp focused open world FPS/TPS MMO amalgamate based in a massive desert wasteland....
The game itself tries to combine open world pvp and the questing PVE environment of MMO's into a single game.
The SKIES system of quest giving is operated through attribute requirements to trigger quests, and dialog responses are managed through a mesurement of your intelligence attribute, making you either sound like either a complete dumbass or the second re-incarnation of cassanova in dialogue. The game's open world pvp can be a turn off for some as a lot of people are worried of being ganked without reason, (See Mortal online) however it does not really matter much as from what I can understand, nothing is lost on death, besides durability which by it self degrades with continual weapon and equipment use. The trade system can also be a little confusing at first as it can have some first time players who may have played games such as fallout and fallout 2 in the past believe that it works like fallout's barter system, however the difference text in this game defines how many coins you will either obtain after trade or lose after trade. The optimization is also pretty buggy near big towns and server shutdowns are regular occurances. The exit to the starting area also tends to be camped by PK'ers attempting to test their luck. However I can definitely see some potential in this Early access Early alpha game even though I am not much of a fan of the open pvp idea.
Pros
-----
- Combat is pretty solid at the time of this review.
- Wasteland 2 style wasteland.
- Both FPS & TPS cameras.

I create my character, looking a bit bland as the character creator is no where near complete. I then spawn into the farm where all new players go. Upon leaving the farm I load in to the sounds of gunshots and running, I notice a white name plate player next to me firing at another white name plate, given my good samaritan status that I feel the need to uphold I fire my shotgun into the back of the firing player, this kills him instantly and gives me the killer debuff turning me into a red-tag player for the next hour. I run to town trying my best to avoid all the PK'ers that were waiting to hunt me and other new players down. Obliteracers is a very fun, fast-paced racing game.
The game controls like most kart racing games, except you all share the same camera. Similarly to Speedrunners, if you fall out of the screen border, you die. However, you can also be killed by weaponry.
There are multiple weapons that allow for strategic play. Mines, slippery liquid, homing missiles and fire out of your sides.
You have the ability to bring up a shield at any time, that will negate any damage you take, but slow you down while you use it. You also have the option to hold up your shield as you drive into a weapon pickup, which will heal you, but in turn destroy the weapon. It's a nice trade-situation that allows you to choose.
My favourite game-modes are the ones where you don't respawn until the next round. This means the race gets more intense as you play. When you are dead, you have the option to skip to the next round if only bots are in play, or aim a crosshair and shoot at any racers you want. This allows you to kill someone who is doing better, to even the playing-field. The interesting thing is, if multiple players are dead, you all control the SAME crosshair. So you're all battling over who to kill, it's quite hilarious.
I should mention how great the multiplayer is by the way. You can play up to 16 players. Bots or humans. With a keyboard, controller or even a smartphone. The system to drop in a new player is quite seamless, and even allows for local & online play at the same time.
There's a career mode if you want to play through something alone, although there isn't really anything that interesting to it in my opinion. It's the same as versus mode but with a bit of funny text at the beginning, and it cycles through maps and game modes.
Something pretty fun is you can activate modifiers for races, which keeps things interesting like  doing reversed controls, or the people losing are a bit faster.
Overall, it's a fun racing game with a very nice art style. I love the characters, the world and the gameplay is quite a blast if you have some people to play with!

Obliteracers is a deceptively fun concept that runs on the novel connectivity and accessible of 16 player local-multiplayer. Rather then racing to the end of the goal, it's all about destroying your opponents in absolute chaos.

Obliteracers is absolutely fun. Playing with friends has been an enjoyable romp and even it's lackluster Career Mode holds up better thanks to the game's insane and chaotic nature being both easy to understand and fun! It's polished and immensely playable, and this is backed up by how accessible it also is.
The game's main hook is that up to 16 people can play at once. Have a phone, or a laptop, or a controller? Whip it out, and you can join in on the action very easily. It's simple, and it's responsive too. Although steering with a mobile device ended up being a disaster, it was otherwise surprisingly responsive. No input lag was experienced whatsoever connecting it with other devices.
Unfortunately, it's single-player side is a bit light, which is fine, but because
servers are going to be peer-to-peer versus being dedicated, the online is going to majorly rely on the amount of people playing. It's career mode is just a bunch of set-up matches and isn't particularly too interesting, or even remotely that large of a challenge. Solo players may be turned off by this, but for those who have a ton of friends/family members to play with, it's the perfect couch game to play.
The amount of game-modes, maps, and characters aren't substantial or large, so I'm hoping the developers will continue adding more content as time comes by. The game modes are fun though, although most of them deviate from the main formula of "kill everybody".
On the bright side, it's mutators keep the matches much more interesting; stuff like "Staying on the floor will kill you" and "Everybody bounces around like a literal pinball" shake a lot of races up, reinventing how to play. I think these mutators are going to really make matches
Presentation-wise, it's decent. It's soundtrack is great to jam out too (if it wasn't constantly looped over and over), it's visuals look nice, and the UI doesn't interfere with the game. The menus are fairly basic but get the job done.
The controls may take some getting used to in general, but one notable issue I have is sometimes it wouldn't respond when I started the race accelerating. It's happened multiple times while playing with a phone, controller, and keyboard.
The combat emphasis on the game isn't just a chaotic mess either. You can put up a shield to keep you invulnerable from attacks but you won't be able to accelerate (And the weapon you're holding will drop). It's a cool mechanism that places a risk in the game; Do you want to try and keep the weapon, and attempt a counter attack? Or do you want to drop the item and shield yourself to prevent total devastation? It makes the game much more interesting then "SPAM ITEMS EVERYWHERE!!!".
The online unfortunately is not that populated. Sometimes, you can find a large game of at least 7 people. Other times, it's as empty as it was before the game came out. It's sorta disappointing that the game didn't gain enough traction, since not everybody is going to be able to invite their friends over all of the time.
Overall, Obliteracers is a great game! It's stuck with a few flaws, some weird optimization/control glitches, and a already dead online, but it's a game that's so damn fun and absolutely chaotic.

The world is vibrant and highly unique, and although similar in concept to their previous title Master Reboot, the execution of the presentation is far superior. The idea of exploring memories itself is quite intriguing and allows for some interesting possibilities. The story that fits alongside the strange world is rather odd, because it’s hard to really say where it’s going in its current stages, due to the lack of explanation thus far. However, the short interactions with the strange being that has popped up a few times have certainly caught my attention and it’s something I would love to see more of.
As for the gameplay itself, it consists of environmental exploration and puzzle solving - this of which is done through the usage of certain abilities you pick up along your way. Currently there is only two however, that being removing and placing objects, and a rewind, pause and play function. How you use these with puzzles is actually quite intriguing, as you are able to cause specific objects to construct themselves or deconstruct before your very eyes, or you can rewind a moving object, pause or play it. The puzzles of which are entirely environmental thus far, meaning the manipulation of objects. I certainly found both of these to be very interesting mechanics, especially when bundled together and I look forward to seeing where they take it... However, there is one major problem with Soul Axiom - it's less than 40 minutes long.
I should elaborate on this, because what is currently there in Soul Axiom is very polished and highly enjoyable, there just simply isn’t very much of it. It simply feels like paying for a pie and being given a single mouthful. Sure, it might be delicious and cooked to perfection, but that’s not what you paid for. Awful metaphors aside, an update post linked on the store page does detail the amount of content that is in the game currently, but the information is nowhere to be found on the store page itself.
In its current state I am personally disappointed with the amount that is currently there for the price that it is. The developers have however promised regular updates and I have full confidence that Soul Axiom will be a unique and highly enjoyable game upon completion, and that is personally what I would recommend waiting for. The fault partially lies within the genre, because can’t have a game of that type, so focused on narrative and exploration, part completed and leading to dead ends. For now, we will have to wait and see where Soul Axiom goes, because while the future looks like a bright one, right now it simply falls flat on its face.

Calling this title a rhythm game is kind of misleading for two reasons. If you go into
expecting that the game wants you to hit the corresponding arrow key right as the colored arrows reach the middle of the screen, then you’ll be having a bad time.
The objective is to actually have your central arrow facing the direction of the incoming arrow when the beat lands, which directly means that you have to orient your own arrow at the very latest a split second before impact. So yes, it’s a rhythm game in the sense that the encroaching arrows always land on the beat, but rhythmic gameplay is not required from the player.
There is however a cardinal sin the game commits by introducing varying speeds between arrows, so you can’t concentrate on the arrows in the order they appear. Some arrows can be slow as molasses and hang on screen for multiple seconds, getting overtaken by arrows that show up later but travel faster. This, coupled with the mechanic where blue arrows switch their trajectory mid-flight, makes it incredibly disorienting when trying to concentrate on which arrow is going to land next. And the reason why I call it a cardinal sin is because the speeds at which the arrows travel also don’t seem to be determined by the rhythm itself, again taking away from the claim of
being a rhythm game. Because the speed of the arrows is also not determined by the background music’s intensity or anything, which incidentally can quite often end up not featuring any percussive sounds, making keeping the rhythm even more difficult for people who aren’t musically skilled.
I can’t in good conscience not recommend a free game, since the most you’ll invest in it is your own time if you’re willing to enjoy a fairly simplistic arcade mechanic. There are things here that I really don’t like, but then again, you might like it better than I did.

First of all, I'm a long time Armored Warfare player. Steam doesn't let you review a game unless you play it on Steam, so I downloaded it a second time (I play with separate client) just to write this review. That's how much I care about this came.
Second, I'm trying to be as honest as I can here, so I tell both the positives and the negatives. You can make your own mind if the games worth a try.
Third, comparisons to other tank based F2P games cannot be avoided, mostly I'm talking about World of Tanks.
By the way. Obsidian made the game, but isn't the developer anymore. Now it's handled by
(Mail.ru).
Positives:
+ Actually a fair F2P business model. AW does not have stupid gold sinks. You can have as many tanks in your garage as you like, no limited slots. Tank crews stick to the tanks, and commanders can move freely between them, so no costly retraining. Gold is mostly used for premium time and premium tanks.
+ Plenty of free premium time from events and daily login bonuses (I hope that's a thing in Steam release too). I currently have about 190 days of unused premium time consumables, though I had a years worth of paid premium before, so they stacked up during that.
+ No gold ammo. It means that you can't pay for more penetration or damage. Ammo upgrades exist but they are only small upgrades and price doesn't skyrocket.
+ Quick progression, or for me atleast it has been quick. There are lot's of events with large bonuses and you can stack your boosters with them. In comparison I have three tier tens in AW while in World of Warships I only have one tier nine and no tier tens, even though I believe I've played more WoWS than AW.
+ Essential features like WoT's Sixth Sense (get a warning when you've been seen) are given for free and not hidden behind stupid long experience grind. This means veterans don't have unfair advantage over new players.
+ In general, no pay-to-win. Even premium tanks get nerfs if they need them (and buffs too). Wargaming take heed, you can nerf premium tanks without lawsuits and demands of refund!
+ Fresh new game mechanics like missiles, smoke, wheeled vehicles and target designation.
+ Three game modes: PvP, PvE and Global Operations (GLOPS) which is large map PvP mode with changing objectives, respawns and some bots thrown in. Especially Global Operation is really fun with no camping (if players just would realize that camping doesn't win games in GLOPS).
+ Extremely varied techtrees without much paper tanks (cannot actually think more than one upcoming tank that didn't have at least a single vehicle built in real life)
+ Dynamic gameplay. More simply put, no super sluggish slow tanks like all WoT heavies (except maybe IS-7 which is a low tier gift premium).
+ Low RNG. You actually hit what you aim at, with pretty much any vehicle.
+ No one-shots. You cannot kill a full health vehicle with one shot, unless you set it on fire and it doesn't use a fire extinguisher fo a while (fires are quite rare anyway). Guess what, KV-2 isn't actually a funny tank, but a stupid lottery machine.
+ No artillery (except in PvE and not on bots). Artillery hasn't been a big problem for me in WoT, and I liked how AW originally implemented it (accurate but low damage), but they removed it from PvP and GLOPS because apparently most players didn't want them at all.
Negatives:
- Bugs. Game breaking stuff get's fixed rapidly, but less serious bugs tend to stick around for a long time. Every major patch seems to break as much stuff as it fixes, though micropatches are quite quick to arrive.
- Poor event management. It's a common joke on forums that 0% of events have worked as advertised. Wrong bonuses, wrong timetables, no counters for event conditions (sometimes they exist, sometimes don't), handing out rewards take forever and so on.
- PvE is currently a bit of a mess. It's too easy in general and every attempt to increase difficulty has been just putting more and more braindead bots in missions. Low tier is mostly ok, but high tier PvE is full of bots that just spam missiles with pixel perfect aim. Missions lack creativity and mostly consist of moving down hordes of bots.
- PvP is more or less just the same as WoT. Too much camping. Balance between vehicles is questionable, main battle tanks are univerally good pick, but other vehicle classes suffer on most maps (balance is better in GLOPS as there is more to do with scouts and snipers).
- Poor PvP maps, and not that great PvE maps either (GLOPS is mostly fine). Too small and too much corridors. There's even a map called Narrows, I kid you not. Unarmored low health vehicles have a hard time surviving.
- Win X games in mode Y requirements in events. This is my pet peeve in F2P games. Please do not make requirements that you cannot fill in every match. Grinding without progress isn't fun.
- Plenty of premiums are just reskins of regular tanks, although that kinda makes them balanced. There are unique premiums also.
- Lot's of great ideas but bad implementation. Good example is commander skill revamp just before steam release. Skill trees are a good idea but why do they have empty slots that don't give skill but take away your points? Why are the trees very similar with each commander? Why are unrelated skills put next to each other so you cannot make a coherent build?
- Low player population. You do get games on weekends and evenings but middle of the week during working hours not so much. But that's what Steam release is here to fix right?
So there you have. To me this is the reason I don't play WoT anymore. After AW WoT just feels so outdated with it's slowness. Please give it a try (and stick around for a while) and make your own mind. Check out the game's
too, they're quite active.

Fairly good game however I do have a few complaints. (ideas at the end of review)
Advantages
1: Songs are very catchy and easy to memorise, but without consistent starting points memorising songs is a next to useless ability.
2: Gameplay is quite solid, and the controls feel very fluid and fast. Not once have I ever died because of the controls, only due to me misreading the arrows. This brings me to my next point, The time you have to react to the arrows is perfect in the earlier levels, but it seems slightly unfair in the later difficulties. I understand that this is to make them harder, but at hard diff I expected slightly more reaction time then the given amount. Just a tiny amount more would make it more fair in my opinion.
3: The game doesn't have an extreme amount of movement and colors in a level, but there is enough going on that you don't tune out or lose focus. There are constantly new colors and movement that keep you engrossed in the game and paying attention to what's on screen at any given time.
Disadvantages
1: Background is fairly distracting in the later levels. For some reason hard diff onwards has a background that changes a lot faster than the previous ones. This could be to make it harder to get a high score, but it changes slightly too fast and irritates my eyes. This means i have to take breaks every so often so i don't hurt my eyes, and causes me to lose my focus.
2: The arrows arent synced up to the music. It isn't clear what beat the arrows actually follow, and more than once i've caught myself trying to time my movements to the music rather than the incoming arrows.
3: The level starts at random points in the song, which i guess is to mix it up so the game doesn't get boring. The problem with this however is that it makes it quite hard to build up muscle memory. This does make sense with the game only having only 4 levels, but i hope when more levels get added this issue is fixed.
4: Lack of levels. Only 4 levels are currently in the game, but it did just come out so im giving it a free pass on this issue. (for now)
Ideas
1: One review made by another user earlier had the idea of the following level design: Instead of trying to get 60 seconds on all levels to unlock the 4th level, maybe getting 60 seconds on easy unlocks another diff called easy 2. After that comes easy 3. This could continue onto normal and hard and the 4th diff. That way the game has quite a few levels and the difficulty ramp up isnt so big, just so the newer players to rhythm games don't find it as hard to progress and develop their skills.
2: While the music isn't bad and actually quite catchy, it isn't exactly memorable. Some of the songs seem like a few random sounds were thrown together. Nothing wrong with electronic songs as they quite fit this game and the rhythm game genre as a whole, But maybe consider adding songs that sound more memorable. Not quite sure how to put it, but some of the songs don't seem to fit that well in my opinion. There are definitely some better songs that would fit well but i can't think of any off the top of my head.
3: Maybe add some sort of reward system? Beating your highscore might get boring after a while. One idea i had is that you could add a point system that rewards you points every 10 seconds for staying alive in the later gamemodes. These points could be redeemed for skin packs that change the background, or customizable backgrounds/arrow colors. If you really want to make money you could add the ability to purchase these points to help support the dev(s).
Conclusion
This is a good game, but the flaws are holding it back more then they should.
However, despite the flaws the game is still fairly decent and has virtually no bugs + better gameplay than a lot of stuff i've seen throughout 2017. I would recommend this because i have high hopes for the dev(s) as they have created a truly great game that I know will go through some great changes.

Squad is an absolutely fantastic EA game. The Devs are dedicated and involved in the community. They release substantial patches on a regular basis (new vehicles, maps/map overhauls, weapons, sound design changes). They put out recaps on a monthly basis showing the community what they're working on and the progress they've made as well as being active on the game's subreddit.
The game's been completely transformed since release in 2015 and all the new content has been added completely for free (looking at you, Ark).
It's on the pricey side for some people, but I genuinely believe it's worth it for the experience you get.

One of the best games I've ever played. If you're a fan of Dwarf Fortress or just a fan of punishing yet rewarding strategy games, this is the product for you. First you must create you own characters, which in the standard scenario are three. You create a character through randomization, which means with each roll you get different skills and capabilities. The game also recognizes relationships, which means that your character could be/get married , be brothers/sisters and become friends or enemies. Each one of these relationships comes with upsides and downsides, and are out of your control. Once you've created your team, you crash land on the spot you've selected and are immediately greeted with a whole host of tasks. Collect and manage resources, form a defendable base, hunt and gather food, manage stress level among your colony to make sure no one goes batshit crazy, form caravans to trade with other colonies and tribes, defend from enemy tribes and colonies (or hell, attack back!) and the list goes on. There is so much to do in this wonderfully crafted game that you'll spend hours playing around with it; even more time if you accout for all of the workshop content!

First and foremost - yes, A Twist of Fate is a fitting conclusion (?for now?) of the Runaway series and a quite good, though not great adventure game on its own, well worth playing.
Now that that's done, onto the game. Pendulo seems to have sorted out most though not all complaints from the original elegantly - yeah, the pixel hunting's there, but items can be highlighted now, which helps. Especially with those parts where two pieces of the shelf, labeled the same can be interacted with separately. The gameplay is typical Runaway trigger-happy affair where you need to examine everything, sometimes multiple times, and, often, try everything without much logic initially, but logically retroactively, and, well, slightly more realistic than some (why would you take random thing A until you really need it). I got stuck maybe 3-4 times, and was helped in all but one case (at the beginning), maybe two, by the in-built, nicely integrated and executed in-game hint system you can access at will. Those "I have no idea what needs to be done" moments are thus reduced to a bare minimum. Muliple users (with password protection) are allowed, so if someone is in need of that (families, roommates, etc), a plus for them.
So, yeah, the game is much more easy than the last two sequels, and also seems to be much shorter. Steam says I spent 10h on the second installment and 5h on this one, only partly due to AToF being easier. "Playing areas" are smaller for the better part, so it's easier, in those (few) moments where you end up just trying to combine everything with everything, to progress. The story is generally well written and more or less satisfying, answering most if not all the questions left hanging in the air after the second installment. The fourth wall is broken multiple times, and self-ironic bits are commonplace, which is cute. Controlling different characters helps too, no stagnation really.
Pendulo's attention to detail (graphical mainly) is even more evident than before - though the TDotT's beautiful tropical blues, greens were what made the game a joy to play (and countered much of the gameplay frustration), the settings here are a bit darker and, perhaps, less enjoyable, but there are unique touches everywhere, from the backgrounds, through some of the characters to hotspot descriptions (multiple for the same thing). At certain points you can just interact with characters for interaction's sake, puzzles that don't help you progress but help with the story and the atmosphere... or to waste time while you think they should somehow take you forward - again, become better in retrospective. Musically - typical Runaway, ambiental stuff more than fitting for the setting, punctured by non-ambiental stuff with vocals that sticks out less than before - the French song in the morgue was especially effective. Professionally done.
All in all, again, a good adventure game that's not without its flaws - mostly gameplay-wise and, but it bears them well, aware of them, remaining in line with its predecessors. Recommended.

The third and best game in the Runaway series. A true masterpiece. Although the first two games sometimes reminded me of Broken Sword (one of the best adventure game series of all time), they were never really on the same level as Broken Sword. Runaway 3 changed that. From the very beginning, it's evident that a lot of work went into every little aspect of this game. Everything from the past games was improved, and many of the annoyances were fixed. Some of the puzzles were still a bit too hard/illogical, but the new in-game hint system was very helpful. In fact, it seems like the developers wanted you to use it (or even forced you to), but that's actually a good thing. It's hard to explain, so I'll just leave it at that.
As a standalone game, Runaway 3 is an excellent adventure game. There are tons of references, jokes, and breaking of the fourth wall that will have you laughing from start to finish. You can ask one character about previous Runaway games. I don't want to spoil anything because his commentary was one of the highlights of this experience, but that alone made this game worth playing. The story also seemed to be much more coherent than previous games, which really helped elevate the quality of the game to a whole new level comparable to the likes of classic adventure games such as Broken Sword, Myst, or Grim Fandango .
In conclusion, this game should be in everyone's wishlist. There's something here for everyone, regardless of whether you have played adventure games before. As always, I recommend playing the previous games in the series, but in this case it's not necessary.

Runaway: A Twist of Fate is a classic point n' click game and the third and final installment of the Runaway Trilogy. After a big disappointment to Runaway - Dream of the Turtle, Twist of Fate brings back the mystery and action that Runaway - A Road Adventure had. The graphics and art have been improved and cinematics are much much better than the first two. Twist of Fate makes up for the fails of Dream of the Turtle.
With Dream of the Turtle leaving the players hanging at the end, Twist of Fate answers the questions that were left in Dream of the Turtle. Giving Twist of Fate two key epilogues: Dream of the Turtle ending and the Twist of Fate finale. Twist of Fate is not entirely dependent on Dream of the Turtle since key events in Dream of the Turtle are well explained in Twist of Fate as a flashback. That's why there isn't much a need to play Dream of the Turtle before playing Twist of Fate but I higly recommend that players should play the first installment, Runaway - A Road Adventure.
Twist of Fate maybe considered as the best among the three since the story plot keeps the player begging for more information on how Brian ended up in that certain situation. WIth a lot of question marks at the beginning, players will be clicking their way to know more. Whenever you get stuck, Twist of Fate has two assisting features: An animated guide and the hotspot displayer. With such features, players won't likely to get frustrated whenever they get stuck on a certain chapter.
Since this one's quite an old game, I recommend it to players that they should buy this when it gets on sale. It's still an Instant Pendulo Studios Classic.

A few years back, Weird Worlds: Return to Infinite Space was recommended to me, and I gave the demo a spin. I was hooked, and played for much longer than I had planned. This space strategy game (some call it Rogue-like) kept calling me to play one more game, and I heeded its call.
Fast forward to the end of 2015 and I finally gave the full game a spin. The familiar menus popped up, the familiar map, and the familiar gameplay all triggered positive memories dating back to when I first played Weird Worlds, not long after building a gaming PC and joining the so-called 'Master Race' for the first time.
The game boils down to these elements:
1) Pick your name, ship name, and type
2) Explore a randomly generated galactic map, complete with barren planets, trading posts, and alien races -- both friend and foe.
3) You must explore as much as you can, bringing back items of monetary and scientific value, before time is up. This limit is imposed on you between steps 1 and 2, and is always on screen. Don't worry, you have plenty of time unless you keep battling enemies, and accidentally hit the forward button a few times like I did.
Battles are, admittedly and unfortunately, rather boring. There isn't much strategic element, and honestly I escaped whenever possible.
Exploration is a little bland, and limited to clicking a world, waiting to see what pops up, and then either trading, dealing with the fallout, or moving on to the next one.
Alpha Centauri or FTL, this game is not.
So what is it? Why recommend it? Well, a game can be played in 15-30 minutes, and if you don't binge on it (thus seeing all it has to offer in one sitting), you can return to it days, months, or years later for another quick trip around the stars, then put it back on the shelf again until next time. In other words, it's a quick palate cleanse in between meatier experiences. It can be neat discovering an interesting race, item, or upgrade for your ship.
It's also dirt cheap, has mod support (note: The Star Wars one I downloaded from the official site locked up my game), and easy to learn, meaning you can play it with casual/non gamers such as youngsters and other relatives and friends.
Know what to expect, and I don't think you'll be let down.

Weird Worlds: Return to Infinite Space is the second part of a series of games.
If you have to describe it with only one paragraph you could say: "It's a Starflight, or Star Controll II light game, with a lot of humorous and casual gameplay."
Actually it's really a casual game, it has permadeath functionality and you will gain scores depending on the in game achievements your captain might gather.
It is fun, if you want to play a short game with some nice flavourtexts about hellworlds, aliens and such notions like... "Don't point that on my planet!"
This game actually can be a lot of fun, as long as you keep in mind that it's a game for in between. A game for small breaks, or if you wait for another session going on...
But if you play this game in a more lasting way, you will soon learn that it get's repetitive, boring and shallow.
So this game is recommendable to people who are on the lookout for a fast speed session, maybe between two raids, or when waiting for the pizza delivery or the doctor after you actually ate the pizza...
Oh, by the way - no aliens were harmed during the test!

The good news is that it seems to have a lot of custom sprites and a mostly consistent aesthetic. You can see the RPGmaker creeping in at the edges, but this isn't an unappetizing kludge of stock sprites. A lot of the visual design mirrors Earthbound, right down to the feel of the fonts, and the soundtrack is similarly in-vein. Unfortunately, where Earthbound was a strangely consistent fever-dream of a gameworld, Red Nightmare feels weirdly bland. It imitates the first impression that Earthbound gives off, but in Red Nightmare's case that impression is skin deep.
The game is fairly big, and it's packed with little details that make it clear a lot of work went into it. There's a day-night system, a calendar, seasons, lots of sidequests, a relatively open main quest...and it's all kind of dragged down by the blandness. Combat doesn't feel great either. Attacks are loaded with special effects, they don't hit for a lot of damage, and everything is an HP sponge. This makes combat real slow, which would be fine if it wasn't absolutely everywhere.
Based on game size and content, this is a steal for a dollar, but based on fun-per-hour I'm not so sure it's worth the investment.
If you really, really liked Nusakana's game-feel, or if you adored Earthbound's visual design/sound design, give this a try.
Otherwise, there are a *lot* of other games out there.

9/10 on PC with Steam
A delightful Rogue-like 2D space exploration adventure; upgrade your ship, collect artifacts, battle alien races, and finish in 30 minutes ! Play this game if you want to level up your procrastination badge.
While ‘The Binding of Isaac’ is pressure-inducing, morally complex, and fast paced with severe depth,  ‘Weird Worlds: The Return to infinite space’ is relaxing, gentle and well circumscribed, the perfect depth for what is promised; a Short break time game permitting escape from the dull beat of the work drum.
Do not read a single FAQ for this game - just enjoy exploring through trial and error. Player skill is increased through successive rounds. Random elements are introduced as the game progresses, so playing the 30 minute version is more interesting than the 20 or 10 minute versions. I wish there was a 60 minute version XD
Negative comments by others include that random generation may produce unfavorable layouts of the universe. The flip side is that at some point your knowledge and experience can negate the random effects and create advantages.
All you need to know:
1. Explore more of the universe by upgrading the FTL drives and navigation computer and avoid getting sucked into a blackhole.
2. Be a space pirate. Upgrade your weapons and thrusters and hire mercenaries.
3. Trade. Alien races will keep you guessing and are the gateway to mercantile opportunities. Trade is organized to facilitate the game and wealth accrual is secondary.
4. Comparing items (thrusters, shields ect) is straightforward and comes down to the coin values (1-5).
5. Experimenting with bizarre artifacts will uncover favorable secrets.
Play this game if you want space exploration with modest effort into depth and prefer short 30 minute conclusions, or
Play this game if you have never played a rogue-like; it is the perfect gentle introduction to the rogue-like genre in a 2D Space exploration format.

Firstly: This is a Free2Play (& not at all Pay2Win) game. The best review comes from YOUR own experience. If you like what you see, give it a try. What've you got to lose?
Anyway, let me tell you what I think about AW after... well getting close to 3 years of playing it now. (via the game's own launcher, not Steam, hence low play hours here)
I've played the game since the very early Alpha days and I have seen it grow. I  have seen it do well, I have seen it in its very worst days. I also engage myself as a Community Moderator and because of my contacts with the game's publisher, I can see the game in a different light than most. That said, my honesty compels me to write an honest review, so here we go.
Overall Rating: 8.5/10
Pro's:
* Great graphics and optimisation
* Good, believable sounds
* Gameplay is fluid and just feels good.
* No Pay2Win, no "garage slots", no "barracks slots", no need for premium at high tiers
* Maps are very varied
* Vehicle lines are also very varied with lots of truly unique ones across the tech tree
* Good tutorial and easy to get started
* Good, stable server connection
* Game itself runs stable, too
* Full Co-op PvE mode (you can perfectly grind the game from tier 1-10 purely in PvE)
* Global Operations mode is a breath of fresh air and a truly different style of play
* Very low RNG
* Good UI (ooh the controversy!)
* Camouflage can be bought permanently for in-game credits
* Very dedicated Dev and publisher team (I know, firsthand)
* Fast speed of development (relatively quick patches)
* High interaction between publisher and players through the forums (Silentstalker ftw)
* Very generous events which are held often (can earn tier 6 premium tanks through reasonable effort for instance)
Con's:
* Lack of endgame / competitive content (though, rumors say next patch may bring both)
* Events can sometimes be troublesome (reward payout delayed, sporadic issues with the tracker page)
* (at time of writing) rather low playerbase (but, you, reading this, can help!)
* Occasional bugs, some bigger, some small. (but let's face it, have what game, doesn't?)
Conclusion: I really like the game, always have. I've got 2200+ PvE, 300+ PvP and 400+ Glops battles and I'm still playing. It's definitely not without issues but the dev team are crazy (in a good way :P) and the speed of development is very good.
I also lead a strong in-game battalion (aka clan) called Angels of Death. I strongly reccomend to, if you like the game, join a battalion. As with any multiplayer game, AW too, is best enjoyed with friends.
If you think you'd like driving around and blowing sh*t up, with (virtual) modern armored vehicles, this game will likely be right up your alley. And it's free, so, why not just give it a try?

Rogue Port - Red Nightmare, while clearly inspired by classics such as EarthBound, does well to hold it's own.
The day/night system, dynamic lighting and randomised loot drops help to give Rogue Port it's own identity.
The battle system is a classic take on the turn based system you'll remember from early Final Fantasy games, with a few more modern inspirations. Approaching the enemy from behind to get the jump on them for example.
The visuals are cutesy and again, hugely EarthBound inspired. The combination of dynamic lighting and a fantastic musical score, does a great job of creating atmosphere, pulling you into the world of Rogue Port.
If you grew up with your mind buried deep inside the huge worlds in games like Final Fantasy, Earth Bound and even Chrono Trigger, then Rogue Port is most certainly for you. If not, you might still be surprised.
It's awesome to see more indie developers working on retro inspired RPGs. The more the merrier, I say.
Go and grab it now.

Oxenfree is one of those games where if you start playing it, you just HAVE to finish it.
I remember getting this game a while ago, when I didn't have a computer it could run on so I used someone elses, I only played for about half an hour, before eventually forgetting about it.
I was scrolling through the Nintendo eShop and saw it available, which led me to download it on my current computer only yesterday, and I played for 4 hours straight, stopped to have dinner, and then finished the game.
The thing about Oxenfree, is you can't play it once. There's multiple endings, and variations od what can happen during the story.
Let me explain the goods and bads of this game:
Pros:
- The Art: The artstyle of this game is beautiful, what else can I say
- The Characters: The characters in this game start off to be not that interesting, but you can develop their personalities more throughout the game depedning on your choices, which can make up some pretty interesting scenarios.
- The Story: I found the story to be really good. Although slow at the start, once you get to the Comm Tower for the first time and learn more about some of the characters, the game gets really interesting.
- The Radio: The radio was a cool aspect of this game, and also one of the most vital points of the game. The radio is used to discover more about the island, as if you tune into a specific radio station at the Tour Stops, you learn more about the backstory which can help you understand some of the story elements a bit more. The radio also helps you complete certain "puzzles."
- The Soundtrack: The soundtrack of this game is good! I have the version of the game that has the soundtrack included, and it's just wonderful. It helps set the scene in certain locations and it's cool when
- The Ending: I'm not going to say anything apart from: I'm shook.
And now,
The Cons:
- The Walking: There's so much walking in this game that it gets frustrating. You go from one side of the map, to end up having to go to the complete other side of the map after doing one simple task.
- The Map: Although you usually have little marks to tell you where to go in the game, sometimes you don't. Sometimes the characters tell you where you need to go one time and then it doesn't set a mark on the map
.
Oxenfree is a great game with a great story. There are "horror" aspects to this game which overall makes a very creepy experience. The game can be unsettling at times, but it makes for a great experience.
I'd highly recommend you buy this game if you are into shows like Stranger Things, DARK or Twin Peaks. Or if you are into games like Life is Strange.

Friend bought this game for me and a couple others, it seemed like a pretty decent looking arcade style game. Roguelike elements which I enjoy, a hardcore mode to make it entertaining, and multiple classes which have both skill and item progression. Sounds awesome right? Wrong.
This game is implemented so poorly that it's not even playable in any aspect. Updates are so far and inbetween and they don't fix anything, it's mind-boggling. Our first experience with the game was loading up a server, after a tedious amount of tinkering we finally were all able to connect, and 1-3 of the players outside of the host would crash after the first few waves. This was consistent, looking to the discussion forums many were having this problem, and the developers met the complaints and requests for assistance with a literal '♥♥♥♥ off coding is hard'.
So the game was placed on the backburner in my mind until a few months later, I just happen to see it on sale once again, and I look at the updates which say multiplayer had been fixed. In fact mutliple patches in a row claim this, this was not the case. If by fixed they meant that players could remain in the game for more than a wave or two, then yes it was fixed, but a new problem arised. At seemingly complete randomness, when someone would level up and allocate skill points, other player's abilities would be replaced or disappear entirely. Control of your character is not common, in fact every game I lost control of my character. All character names were replaced with a single player's name, and level up stats seemed to be utterly broken. There were even times when other people were controlling my character. Once again, mind boggling how this even happens, but ask the developers what's up and you're berrated.
Is there a playable game here? Maybe, if they ever get the multiplayer up and running, but in all honestly the game is so shallow that single player is out of the question for me at least. It's riddled with bugs, the gameplay itself isn't all that entertaining, and while on the surface there seems to be replayability and depth there really isn't. Skill trees are bland and boring, stat points pretty much only enhance a single attribute, but most importantly the actual playing of the game is done poorly. WASD to move, arrow keys to shoot in a direction. You cannot shoot in other directions, just up down left right, which very quickly removes any and all strategy to the game at all.  Graphics are done well for what they're trying to accomplish, but that's about the only praise I can offer.
Even if they offered this game for free I wouldn't bother. It's so broken and unplayable in multiplayer that they should be paying us to test and offer feedback. It's so bland and repetitive in single-player that I won't even touch it.

I seldom review games I've only played for an hour or less, because I do not feel I can judge a game solely on just that time. QuestEvent is a different story, as it is not only not longer than an hour, but I also managed to formulate an opinion on it. TL;DR it's an unfinished mess.
Let me start right off that I've been playing Runescape for well over 10 years now. Why did I bring this up? Because QuestEvent has no shame in ripping off everything that mmo has to offer, just laughably bad. The content that we've seen so far is something I, an inexperienced game developer, could do in less than a day. There is ONE city, TWO quests which are laughable, and FIVE skills that serve absolutely no purpose.
Want me to go in detail? Sure. In Runescape, certain trees and fishing spots are unlocked at specific levels so you are able to get resources from them. For example, you can cut Oak Trees at level 15, and Willow at level 30. Well, how about QuestEvent having that EXACT same levelling method, and not only for Woodcutting but all of the other skills as well? And to make matters even worse, the icons of the fish in the inventory AND the level-up sound are all directly stolen from Runescape.
Want to go even further? Dungeoneering. A fun skill to do in Runescape since it's literally Roguelike dungeon crawling. Everytime you enter, you face the challenge of a different layout. How much dungeons does QuestEvent have? ONE! And it never changes either!
I feel like I should complain about the city as well, and the stuff you can get there since there are no stronger monsters to defeat than the one found in Dungeoneering, but I think you get the point I wanted to get across. QuestEvent is an unfinished, soulless game that has been put together in a few hours, and put unto Steam to rob you of your precious money. Yes, this 'game' is not even worth the 3 dollar pricetag.
I wrote this review because I get what QuestEvent was going for, and really, I'd love to see a single-player game based on Runescape. But this is not the way to go. Get this off Steam, put in far more effort, and until that time happens, we will not meet again.

I really liked the idea and concept of the game that you can level four skills which - for a change - don't have anything to do with killing monsters. Unfortunately, the game development got cancelled in favor of a new project and that leaves a rather bad impression as this game is in no way a finished product.
You can finish this game within 20 to 30 minutes exploring everything and considering you have to grind the fire making skill to level 15 (wood cutting before, I think), so in my opinion it's not really worth the money it costs. Of course, the music is really nicely done and catchy, the few characters look quite nice as well and nobody is stopping you from grinding all your skills (four in total) to the highest level (apparently level 99). However, to be honest, I got rather bored with that after a while and I won't continue to play the game just to level my skills higher.
Overall, the game had a lot of potential to be a fun and entertaining experience to enjoy but it got cut short because of the cancellation. Otherwise I would have given it a positive review as it belongs to the sort of games I really like to play and I can easily overlook the spelling and grammar mistakes as English isn't my native language either.

Bad Game, Bad Developer, Just Another Generic RPG Maker Game.
Short~
I'm not even an RPG Fan, I didn't even ask for the game.  I also haven't played Earthbound. This is just another RPG Maker Game on Steam but with a coat of paint covering its stale pre-done engine that jumped on the Underbound train.  Only Undertale was made with Game Maker, has a story worth following and doesn't depend on a stale turn-based combat system.
Long~
The Story!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
The intro/story is poorly explained, right from the start you choose your characters name and class along with the other friends and your dog after that all you get is a few sentences of dialog that "explains" the story.  After that you get a very limited selection of choices that will effect your starting stats.......then a meteor crashes in the town and your friends are kidnapped.  From then on its just doing random quest that are just joined together with very little dialogue.
The Gameplay!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
You walk around (you can also run as well) on the over world like every other RPG Maker Game, the only difference is that the battle changes depending on which direction you face the enemy, the battles are simple enough during the intro sequence while in the house, but don't be surprised if you die right after leaving the house, which also leads to a terrible choice the developer made.
At No Point Are You Told That The Phone Saves Your Progress
So after making your characters and going all the way through the intro and making your character....you die and lose your progress. all of it~
And the save button is grayed out in the menu.  I actually had to ask the Dev about this and waited a few days for a response.  By that point I was pretty sick of this game and really couldn't see any difference between this and any other crappy RPG Maker Game that I have seen on Greenlight.
THE GRAPHICS!!!!!!!!!!
Widescreen in 2016 - Nope!!!!!!
Full screen - Yes, but its not adjustable ingame with an option screen or anything like that.  You had to use Alt-Enter to adjust it in early versions, but now F1 brings a generic RPG Maker text box up with limited setting including start in full screen.
Blury Graphics in Full Screen Mode - But Of Course~  It even makes the text nearly unreadable at times.
The Graphics - Very Mediocre~  Every character looks the same but with different hair and clothes, the enemy sprites look okay, but have been scaled up and look very pixelated.  The battle background have the same distorted look that Earthbound has and honestly don't look good at all, I'm sure that the code for that effect is either already in the RPG Maker Engine or was just found on a forum/tutorial.
I didn't enjoy my experience with this game nor with dealing with the Developer.

Very fun and engaging, requires a fair bit of muscle memory and reaction timing to place the direction of your arrows to the corresponding ones. Much like a dance arcade game, this functions similarly in that you have to time the arrow to the patterns of the music.
Be warned, the tempo of the modes above do get very tricky. And once it's game over, you have to try again and again to beat your score. This IS a game of survival. But don't be fooled by how monotonous that sounds, the soundtracks are very captivating even if you're not a fan of dance music, and they don't fully reset every time you make another effort to beat your score - so it does try to make each attempt different, especially with the RNG of the arrows and their speeds. Much of the theme of the actual gameplay seems very reminiscent of the Undyne boss battle from Undertale where you have to guard against the attacking arrows and have to switch sides from the blue ones. Which can catch you off guard a lot.
For a free game, this is definitely a must-try. The animations are perfect, the sounds are great and the visuals are colourful and captivating. There is complete controller functionality involved, too - if you have one. As well as rumble. Although, if you suffer from dyslexia or hypersensitivity, then the arrows, the bright colours and the animations might be a bit much. That being said, this is a great, challenging game and a fun past-time to get stuck in with if you're bored and in need of a buzz.
8/10
EDIT: One thing that does bug me, though, is the fact that the game isn't skill-based or based off of a score of how many arrows you managed to get in the time you had. Because every arrow is randomised and with it being a time-based score system, it's hard to get into the grips with the level of difficulty at times with how many arrows are being thrown at you from all directions. The arrows can be paced differently which can screw with your mind. So you either have the attention span and reaction time of a god, or you legitimately need to get better each time.
Another thing is that there doesn't seem to be any ranked system. Like an online scoreboard where you can share your time with your friends, etc. But as said previously, this game at its current state seems to be a pure past-time. And for a game that's free, this is what you get. So it's not all that bad.

I have been playing this game since before OBT. I had gotten into it because it was talked up as a game that was going to have an emphasis on PvE (as in being equal to PvP in focus) and deeper and more RPG like systems outside of the matches. This fit the MO of the developer at the time, which was Obsidian Entertainment. However, what was given was something that felt like a faster World of Tanks with little depth. It had interesting ideas such as the base system, but that was scrapped instead of being developed more. A commander system that was very shallow (even the new commander system is shallow compared to what OE had on the Wiki) and consistently messed up and weak specials and events when compared to the Russian server.
They like to say the game is still in Beta, yet testing exploits to send an actual proper bug report will get you banned. They also have a fully functioning shop. Nothing around it feels like a beta, except for all the unfished features in the game.
A great example of the horrid events they have for us. The anniversity of the game happened recently and said that we'd get a gift tank as appreciation for playing the game. Now, previously a gift tank was given for almost no effort or time investment on the day of the event. This time however? It required double digit victories in GLOPs or PvP, completely ignoring PvE. The issue is that it ignores something they say they want to treat as equal, and that the queues for GLOPs and PvP are terrible due to population issues from people leaving. It was hardly a gift. On eth Russian server, all they had to do was do any amount of damage in any game mode, it was an actual gift.
There have been numerous events that have failed to start on time, ended early, rewards from the events often failed to get delivered
Despite OE being listed as a developer, they are not involved with the game. Apparently what OE wanted was not what
, I mean Mail.ru wanted. Mail.ru wanted a WoT clone. You can see this more and more since OE has left. The UI was changed from something that admittedly needed work to a UI that looks nice but lacks usability for a PC game and looks surprisingly similar to World of Tanks. The Tank trees suddenly switched from vertical to horizontal, much like WoT. Even in gameplay things have been becoming more like WoT. Modern tanks have gradually been moving closer and closer to the old tanks found in WoT. Tanks with stabalizers suffer massive bloom on the move. It no longer feels like I'm driving a modern tank. War Thunder pulled off modern tanks as an April Fools better than this game pulls it off.
And again, they have said they want PvE to be equal to the PvP modes but the current campaign greatly favors the PvP modes. they try and use events to force people into PvP despite comments that they do not want people to have to play something they don't want to. This has the effect of temporarily fixing queues, but also♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the PvEer who kept the game alive, despite being largely ignored.
PvE modes are pretty bland. Nothing has been done to really improve them. The AI is brainless objectives are rudimentary. Just feels like it exists so they can say they have PvE that their competitors do not.
likes to blame OE for the shortcomings, but since OE has left, the quality has not improved, and it is just becoming more and more like WoT.
My entire reason for not recommending the game is because of the people running it. 'Tales from the Borderlands'; 2014, Telltale Games and Gearbox Software.
Tales from the Borderlands is an episodic adventure game that is a real standout from the previous installments in the Borderlands franchise. Unlike Borderlands, Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel, and Borderlands 2, Tales from the Borderlands is all about your choices in the game and how they influence the story. This is very much in the style of games like Mass Effect where a simple decision early in the game may and probably will influence the ending. Note the phrase 'simple' in the previous sentence as something as minor as fistbumping a loader bot could screw you over.
As stated before, this game does not rely on action-packed shoot-outs like prior installments, however, this does by any means that the game is boring or that different from the others. Telltale Games did a fantastic job in sticking true to the Borderlands universe as the game is full of pop culture references, interesting stories, and above-all, comedy. This game has some seriously funny moments in it which for fans of Borderlands, should not be so unfamiliar.
Episode 3: Catch a Ride has not yet been released, but I cannot wait. I've already prepared myself to go through the story again and change the way I did things and re-experience some of the moments. For true Vault Hunters, you will know all about replaying the game.  Telltale Games really hit it out of the park with this and this game has only extended my love of the Borderlands franchise.

is an adventure RPG game heavily inspired by various
16-bit titles (such as Earthbound and Pokémon).
The game plays similar to other games made in
: You have your main quest (which is rescuing your friends), various sidequests scattered around the world, monsters roaming everywhere you go, standard stuff. However, there are a lot of little things that make this game different from your normal RPG Maker game, like stamina bar (more stamina means more sprinting time), day and night system with dynamic music, calendar system, pretty dynamic lighting effect, character customization (every piece of apparel that you equip changes your sprite), and so on.
There are quite a lot of different places to visit, like towns, caves, and forests. A lot of those locations don't have anything to do with the main quest, but It's wise to explore them anyway, as they commonly contain hidden treasure chests and key items for sidequests.
They are really, really good (for a game made in RPG Maker, duh!). You won't see any sprites ripped directly from RTP packages, like in other RPGM games here on Steam. As previously said, game has a nice dynamic lighting effect, meaning that the light changes depending on location and time. Character and enemies sprites are all nicely made (bonus points for animating them).
RPG Maker standard: Arrow keys to move, Shift for sprint, Esc for opening up the menu, Space for everything else. Those are standard controls in those kinds of games, because they are comfortable to use. If you don't like them for some reason, there's a remapping menu available under the F1 key.
Sound effects are fitting in most situations, so is music. I liked how it changes depending on time of the day, exploring the forest in the middle of the night is much more chilling because of that. But, no matter how great the music is, it still wouldn't hurt to implement the mute option within the game.
One of the best RPG Maker games I've played. Developer put a lot of work in this small indie title, didn't take any shortcuts by using default sprites and music, and for that sole reason this game is already better than 75% of other RPGM titles, at least in my book.

First things first:
Despite negative review, give this game a good shot. It needs players so it does not take forever to get into battles. And once it has players, devs might start to pay more attention to us because it is not a horrible game, it can be fun, it is not P2W and it does not punish you for not paying. It just does not meet its potential, yet.
Just want to ask you one thing, dont throw your wallet at them right from the beginning. Premium account is all you will need up to tier 7. Lets see what they will do with the game once they have ppl playing it.
Now for my opinion/ review:
Long time player here. Had a break for a couple of months because the game development did not move anywhere in a long time and player base died out for lack of end-game content and below 10 new progress vehicles in over a year time. However, I played last 2 days, with the newest update 0.22, just to see if the game moved in the good direction. And I have to say that it did not, not really.
Just to point out, I am writing this as a pure PVP player. I do not care or know anything about the state of PVE. Played 2 PVE battles yesterday on Hard and it is a walk in the park for me which is boring.
Pros:
- very low accuracy RNG and I really mean very low, where you aim, there it goes! (gets better the higher you go)
- no need to pay a penny, this game really does not force you to do so (premium account is always welcome, but thats it), you will do well without paying until high enough tier to know whether you want to or not...
- new commanders system from 0.22 is good, it finally gives at least some end game incentive... even tho most skills are useless, but you can find that in every game
- anti-camp spotting mechanics - I say more about spotting in cons, but this is a good part... the more you shoot, the higher penalty to camo you get which means you can never stay one spot long OR you have to take a break to "refill" your camo...
Cons:
- vehicle physics is terrible, they made close to 0 progress from what it used to be 2 years ago and it still feels like a physics from 2005 game, you can probably find better in some mobile games
- vehicles which are obviously OP AF spread across all tiers and should never be in game in their current state because even the worlds blindest person would notice how unbalanced they are (MIND MOST OF THEM PROGRESS VEHICLES, NOT PREMIUMS, SO NOT P2W)
- map design is no good, the best maps are the really old ones and even there you can find bits which look and feel terrible, new maps are just overcomplicated, and you will get lost even after playing tens of battles
- destruction of objects - it is really sad to say that newer the map, the fewer objects which you can destroy... it gets really annoying in those maze like maps...
- spotting mechanics - they made a good progress compared to what it used to be, you can see some difference in class roles in this area, however the map design will make you go nuts with all the corridors where non MBT class vehicles can do just one thing and that is to count on the stupidity of the enemy to go somewhere open so you have something to do in battle...
- UI - in my opinion the new look is great, however I say it is a con because it is just another unfinished part of this game, you can still find OLD UI bits popping everywhere + it is buggy, you can pick a tank click battle and end up with different tank in the battle, and also things they promies specially for post battle screen is still not there, mainly you can not see other people stats in detail... (probably just my personal con as I am a competitive player and would love to see that kind of information)
- still NO END-GAME CONTENT - and I know you, as new players, wont really care about end-game yet, but just so you get the picture, this game has been out* for over 2 years now, They promised Lords Of War (was supposed to be first end-game step) a 1,5 year ago. To this date it is still not in game...  Still no Battalion content...
- killing the competitive aspect - you can not have MMO game without some kind of competitive part, this game has nothing, you have literally 0 motivation to improve, because you have nobody to compare with since everyone can just hide their stats and you have no ranks or anything else...

The game is OK for an adventure game, however, it has its flaws.
I could not get dragged into the story at all, as I did not cared too much about the main characters. The game starts with the fake funeral of the series main character. The further you get into the game the more plot holes you might spot. As usual in these kind of games, you march on by stealing from people, and distracting people.
Humour is a main part of the game, with a lot of jokes referring to pop culture, e.g. the swap scene in Raiders of the Lost Ark as seen in the promo video. Somehow, these jokes fell flat to me.
Puzzles are of the dialogue and inventory types and no logic or mathematics puzzles. There are only two actions to take on each hotspot on the screen: look and use. Some of the solutions are odd, and some of the situations that arise from those solutions are too. For example, combining a large stick with a ribbon and a disc cutter in order to be able to  remotely cut through steel probably does not work in real life. Not every item in the inventory needs to be used.
Hints are provided in-game, and these ones are often useful. Hotspot locations are highlighted at the press of the F2 key. My main gripe with the game is that some screen transitions are not hinted by the mouse cursor. First example of that happens on the second chapter, where you enter a large room. If you click in a nowhere region, you then can see another section of the room. I felt the lack of hotspot in these cases confusing.
Graphics are crisp and vivid, with characters being prerendered. There is an over emphasis on using video.
Voice is everywhere in this game, with lots of extra dialogue that might not end in anything. Many items do even have two different descriptions. Voice acting in spanish was OK, although two or three different lines were spoken with wrong effects being applied, e.g. talking through a telephone was not consistant.
Technically speaking, the game handles screen resolution in an odd manner. The game is drawn at a single resolution, but allows you to change it. A graphical artifact appeared when I used my screen native resolution - two cursors were shown, one for the location at the native resolution and another for the position of the unscaled game resolution.
As a concluding remark, this game is an OK game to me. There was nothing too good or too bad that could deter other people from playing it.

Runaway: A Twist of Fate concludes the Runaway trilogy, giving it a worthy ending. There are already plenty of good reviews, so I'll just leave some short remarks.
As for the trilogy, this is by far it's best part. Part 1 had absolutely awful puzzles, while Part 2 although it had better puzzles, lacked pacing and failed in the story (telling) department. A Twist of Fate furthermore increased the puzzle quality and the puzzles became a mostly natural part of the story. Setting, story, dialogue, "acting" and pretty much everything got a more professional touch. Additionaly, stuff like hotspots marker and fast walking got added to the game, making it alot less frustrating.
Overall I enjoyed playing the game. Even though it might not be perfect (e.g. sometimes it's very hard to see the indication to skip scenes), it's a game I would recommend every fan of the genre. Chapter 3 was one of the best parts I've ever played in any adventure/p&c game.
I did not like part 1 & 2 of the trilogy and I'd recommend only getting part 3, as in-game dialogue and cut-scene supply you with the needed background information.
Too bad this was the last part of the series. Judging by the progress they made over the trilogy, the next part might've been a masterpiece.
